events.text:
## Summary

**Specification submitted:** Short position in feature 36 (single feature, weight -1), in-sample annualized Sharpe = **1.6068** (net of costs).

**Process:**
1. Declared three stopping triggers up front: stop if best-so-far Sharpe exceeds 1.2, restart after 2 consecutive failures, stop if last gain is negligible (≤0.02).
2. Skipped `pick_prior` — I had no data-independent conviction about any of these 40 anonymized features, so a prior would have been arbitrary.
3. Called `init`, which anchored on the best single feature out of 80 candidates (40 features × 2 signs) and immediately returned Sharpe 1.6068 — already exceeding my 1.2 stop bar.
4. Honored my pre-declared trigger and called `stop` rather than continuing to search, which would have meant changing the rule after seeing a favorable result (explicitly flagged in the rules as a decision "about the data").

**Out-of-sample prediction:** mean Sharpe 0.55, sd 0.45.

**Reasoning for the discount:** An in-sample Sharpe obtained as the best of 80 candidate sign/feature combinations carries substantial selection bias even from a single move. I did not compound this with further search (no `extend_best`/`swap_worst`/`pick`), which limits — but doesn't eliminate — overfitting risk. I shrunk my OOS estimate to roughly one-third of the in-sample value and used a wide standard deviation to reflect genuine uncertainty about how much the edge decays out of sample, given no cross-validation was performed and no independent rationale (economic or structural) for why feature 36 should predict returns.
